title: Module 6: Advanced Analytics (CEP & Views)
content: Welcome to Module 6! 🚀
Today we explore how AMPS transforms raw data into real-time insights.
Topics covered:
• Views & Projections
• Aggregation & Grouping
• Real-time Conflation
• Out-of-Focus (OOF) Notifications
speakerNotes: Introduce the module on analytics and CEP.

title: What are AMPS Views?
content: Views are 'Virtual Topics' calculated from one or more SOW topics.
They act like Materialized Views in a database.
Features:
• Recalculated automatically on every update.
• Can aggregate data (SUM, AVG, etc.).
• Can project (rename/filter) fields.
• Can join data from multiple topics.
speakerNotes: Explain the concept of views as materialized virtual topics.

title: View Data Flow
content: Data flows from Underlying Topics into the View Topic.
AMPS handles the heavy lifting of recalculation.
mermaid:
graph TD
    A[Topic: Orders] -->|Update| V{View: TotalSales}
    B[Topic: Prices] -->|Update| V
    V -->|Real-time| S1[Subscriber A]
    V -->|Real-time| S2[Subscriber B]
speakerNotes: Use the diagram to show how multiple topics feed into a single view.

title: Aggregation Functions
content: AMPS provides powerful built-in functions for data reduction:
• SUM(field): Total value.
• AVG(field): Mean value.
• MIN / MAX(field): Range limits.
• COUNT(field): Number of records.
• COUNT_DISTINCT(field): Number of unique values.
• ANY(field): Returns one example from the group.

title: Grouping and Projection
content: To aggregate data, you must define how to group it.
Any field in the projection that is NOT aggregated becomes part of the 'Grouping Key'.
Example: Grouping by 'Symbol' to get total volume per ticker.
AMPS produces a unique SOW record for each unique grouping key.
speakerNotes: Explain how grouping works similar to SQL GROUP BY.

title: Joining Topics
content: AMPS supports Joins between SOW topics.
• Relationship is defined via a Join expression.
• Format: [TopicA].[Field] = [TopicB].[Field].
• Different message types can be joined (e.g., JSON to FIX).
• This is a LEFT OUTER JOIN: TopicA is the primary; TopicB is the lookup.
speakerNotes: Explain how joins work between topics.

title: Join Behavior
content: If a match is found in the joined topic, fields are merged.
If no match is found, fields from the joined topic appear as NULL.
mermaid:
graph LR
    P[Primary Topic] -- Join Key --> L[Lookup Topic]
    P -- No Match --> O[Result: Primary + NULLs]
    P -- Match --> M[Result: Merged Record]
speakerNotes: Explain the LEFT OUTER JOIN behavior.

title: Real-time Conflation
content: Conflation manages high-update volume for slow consumers.
Instead of every update, subscribers receive the 'latest state' at a specific interval.
• Benefits: Reduced network traffic, prevents client overload.
• Accuracy: Clients always see the most recent data (no staleness beyond the interval).
speakerNotes: Introduce conflation as a solution for high-frequency updates.

title: Subscription Conflation
content: Requested via subscription options (e.g., conflation=1s).
Types of Conflation Control:
• Time-based: Interval (e.g., 500ms, 10s).
• Key-based: Uses SOW keys (or custom conflation_key) to identify 'the same record'.
• Auto-conflation: AMPS adjusts based on client speed.
speakerNotes: Explain the different ways to configure conflation on a subscription.

title: Out-of-Focus (OOF) Notifications
content: What happens when a record no longer matches your filter? 🔍
Without OOF: The client 'loses track' of the record (it just stops updating).
With OOF: AMPS sends a special message notifying the client that the record is gone.
Crucial for maintaining an accurate local cache.
speakerNotes: Explain the purpose of OOF notifications.

title: OOF Reasons
content: AMPS provides a reason code in the OOF header:
• deleted: The record was explicitly removed from the SOW.
• expired: The record's TTL (Time-To-Live) was reached.
• filter: The record was updated and no longer matches the subscription's filter.
• entitlement: The subscriber no longer has permission to see the record.
speakerNotes: Explain the different reason codes for OOF messages.

title: OOF + Conflation
content: What if a record goes out of focus and back in within the same interval?
• AMPS sends the 'final state' at the end of the interval.
• If it's still in focus, no OOF is sent.
• If it's gone at the end, one OOF is sent.
This ensures consistency without excessive noise.
speakerNotes: Explain the interaction between OOF and conflation.

title: Summary: Advanced Analytics
content: • Views provide server-side aggregation and joining.
• Aggregations (SUM, AVG) require Grouping keys.
• Conflation reduces update rates for efficiency.
• OOF notifications are vital for state synchronization.
speakerNotes: Summarize the key points of the module.
